question_en:
We are preparing a parent-child natural history display board titled "How painters depict the inside of fruits." The attachment is one of the illustration plates. Please answer the following questions:

1. Among all color illustration plates in the digitized volume containing the attachment, which plates depict fruits that are cut open, split, or have an opening, clearly showing the internal flesh or seeds? Please list all plate numbers. Plates showing only whole fruits, flowers, pod outlines, leaves, or surface damage to the fruit skin are not counted. What are the common English name and modern scientific name of the plant depicted in each matching plate?

Answer format: Use a table to list item by item the plate number, common English name, and modern scientific name for all matching plates; there is no need to provide a separate list of plate numbers.
answer:
(1)

| Plate No. | Common English Name | Modern Scientific Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | wild soursop | Annona sericea Dunal |
| 9 | pomegranate | Punica granatum L. |
| 14 | soursop | Annona muricata L. |
| 15 | watermelon | Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai |
| 19 | guava | Psidium guajava L. |
| 21 | yellow granadilla | Passiflora laurifolia L. |

| 26 | cacao | Theobroma cacao L. |

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 8-3-D02

## Step 01 · Read the visible composition of the natural history plate

**Action**: Observe the plants and insects in the current attachment; do not assume peripheral scenes or old captions remain visible; example query: Merian pineapple insects Metamorphosis insect Surinam 1705 plate.

**Evidence Observation**: The current image mainly shows a whole pineapple, long leaves, and insects, with no book title or plate number. It provides a clue for matching images in a natural-history volume. The texture of pineapple skin is not the interior of a cut-open fruit, and identifying the input image does not automatically make it a qualifying result.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/129308

https://archive.org/details/Metamorphosisin00Meri

**Result of this step**: Match the pineapple insect image to Plate 1 of the Merian volume.

## Step 02 · Identify the fixed digitized volume

**Action**: Combine BHL item129308 with the Internet Archive fixed identifier Metamorphosisin00Meri to read the volume's bibliography and file list.

**Evidence Observation**: The archive locks the 1705 Metamorphosis volume. An automated download attempt for the BHL entry on 2026-08-10 returned a 403, so this page does not claim successful preservation; the Internet Archive project page, metadata, and the 196-page PDF constitute verifiable volume evidence.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/129308

https://archive.org/details/Metamorphosisin00Meri

https://archive.org/metadata/Metamorphosisin00Meri

https://archive.org/download/Metamorphosisin00Meri/Metamorphosisin00Meri.pdf

**Result of this step**: Continue using the preserved volume content; do not mix in other versions or scattered rephotographs.

## Step 03 · Reconstruct the complete set of 60 color illustration plates

**Action**: Read each color illustration plate by mapping the preserved PDF page numbers, excluding explanatory text and front matter.

**Evidence Observation**: Plate 1 is on PDF page 12, followed by one plate every 3 pages thereafter, i.e., PDF page = 12 + 3 × (Plate No. − 1), up to Plate 60 on PDF page 189. All 60 candidates come from the same fixed PDF; no external direct links to individual images were preserved, so specific PDF page locations are used below without fabricating image asset addresses.

**Evidence Links**:

https://archive.org/download/Metamorphosisin00Meri/Metamorphosisin00Meri.pdf

**Result of this step**: Freeze the complete closed set of Plates 1–60.

## Step 04 · Define visible evidence of opened fruits

**Action**: First determine that the subject is a fruit, then look for cross-sections, splits, or openings where flesh or seeds are discernible inside.

**Evidence Observation**: Whole fruits, flowers, external pod outlines, leaves, and surface damage do not count; cut tuberous roots also do not count. Fruits need not be artificially cut open; naturally split capsules exposing seeds upon ripening also satisfy the condition.

**Evidence Links**:

https://archive.org/download/Metamorphosisin00Meri/Metamorphosisin00Meri.pdf

**Result of this step**: Treat both organ type and internal visibility as conditions.

## Step 18 · Map Historical Plates to Modern Identifications

**Action**: After determining the visual set, consult the 2016 facsimile edition's modern identification table and the 2023 research summary by plate number, avoiding the approach of selecting edible plants first and then reverse-engineering the visual evidence.

**Evidence Observation**: Text on historical plates may use old names; the modern identification table provides the correspondence between plates and modern taxonomy. English common names do not all have unified standards; for plates 3 and 43, follow the preserved research by adopting translations of historical/local names; for plate 23, identification is reliable only to the genus Musa, so retain Musa sp.
